title: Three colours on one emitter
body: A student uses an evacuated tube with a photosensitive emitter C and a collector A. She illuminates C, in turn, with monochromatic light of three frequencies nu1 < nu2 < nu3, all above the threshold frequency of the emitter, and adjusts the source each time so that the intensity of the light reaching C is the same. For each frequency she varies the potential of A with respect to C, from a large positive (accelerating) value down through zero to negative (retarding) values, and records the photocurrent on a microammeter. With a large accelerating potential the current stops rising and stays constant. With a retarding potential the current falls and becomes zero at a sharply defined value of the collector potential, which is different for each of the three frequencies. She plots the three curves of photocurrent against collector potential on the same axes.
